newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Holyman shares adrift on Europe concern.
newsitem.headline: Holyman shares adrift on Europe concern.

text.p: Shares in Holyman Ltd fell 6.25 percent or 25 cents to A$3.75 on Wednesday due to market scepticism about the ferry operator's expansion into Europe, traders said.

The drop to its lowest price since August 14 last year followed a four percent fall last Thursday when the company warned of reduced 1997 expectations for its Holyman Sally operations between England, Belgium and France.
Holyman also said on Tuesday evening that calendar 1997 net profit was likely to be between A$14-A$16 million against last year's A$21.86 million, citing Holyman Sally as a major factor.
The company said it had reduced its 1997 expectations for its 66 percent-owned Holyman Sally European ferry operation after a review of its performance.
Brokers said the bad news on Europe was still filtering back to Australia, prompting the latest price fall.
"That news is still being felt through the market and they've taken a further hard hit," said one senior dealer at a Sydney broker.

Tuesday's announcement that Holyman had agreed in principle with Brierley Investments Ltd to buy the Australian shipping business of Union Shipping Group for A$58.3 million had had little impact, brokers said.
Holyman was a division of transport group TNT Ltd before it was floated in April 1994.
Brokers said the market was showing that initial high expectations for the group may have been unrealistic.
"There was a fair premium factored into their price and that premium is being eroded," a Sydney dealer said.
